sentences.text:
This is an application under Section 439 Cr.P.C.
 2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and  learned counsel for the State.
 3.

The petitioner is an accused in connection with  Muribahal P.S. Case No.325 of 2023 corresponding to  Special G.R. Case No.101 of 2023 registered under Sections 363/366/376(2)(n) of the I.P.C. read with Section 6(1) of the POCSO Act pending in the Court of  leaned Special Judge (POCSO), Balangir.
4. The prosecution case is that, on 29.11.2023 at  5.00 A.M., the daughter of the informant fled away  from the house without giving information to any one.

Then the informat and his relatives searched for her,
 but unable to trace her out.
The informant suspected that his daughter has fled away with the petitioner.

Hence, the F.I.R.
5.
Learned counsel for the State submits that during investigation, the statement of the victim, who was aged about 17 years then, has been recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.
In her statement, she inter alia stated that she has been in relationship with the petitioner, who was aged about 19 years.
She on her own will accompanied the petitioner and stayed together.
During their stay at Sambalpur, they kept physical relationship.
Her family members rescued her from the custody of the petitioner and F.I.R. was registered.

6. The bail plea of the petitioner was rejected on 22.03.2024 by the learned trial Court.
7. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the plea of bail of the petitioner is not pending before any other Court, except the present one.
8. Taking into consideration the period of custody since 19.12.2023, the nature of accusation and the fact that the petitioner was aged about 19 years, I am inclined to admit the petitioner on bail.

The prosecution is given liberty to move application before the Court below for cancellation of bail,
if the petitioner violates any of the conditions of the bail granted to him.
9. The BLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
(S.S. Mishra) Judge amit Location: HIGH COURT OF ORISSA, CUTTACK Subham Chhura vs State Of Odisha .... Opp.
